picks.rationale: Strongest pick: a generative-AI capability landing natively in the NLE most of the industry already cuts in — prompt-to-video and prompt-to-SFX directly on the Premiere timeline, a real day-to-day editing/finishing change. Distinct from the already-published Premiere Color Mode card (that was tonal/UI; this is generative).
picks.excerpt: Scott Simmons details Premiere's new (beta) Generative Media Tool, which lets editors create generative video and sound effects directly in the timeline by dragging across empty space or double-clicking to type a prompt — Adobe's continued generative-AI push inside the dominant NLE.

picks.rationale: Infrastructure that reshapes how AI-film tools get built: one model-agnostic API to wire frontier image/video/audio/character models (Gen-4.5, Aleph 2.0, Act-Two, plus third-party Seedance, GPT Image 2, ElevenLabs) into bespoke filmmaking pipelines, swappable in one line. Chosen over Runway Seed Audio — same vendor, bigger story, keeping Runway to one pick.
picks.excerpt: Runway Dev is a new AI media platform for developers: a single API to integrate the best image, video, audio and real-time character models, giving access to Runway's frontier models (Gen-4.5, Aleph 2.0, Act-Two) alongside third-party models like Seedance, GPT Image 2 and ElevenLabs, swappable by changing one line of code.

picks.rationale: Included to round out the deck: a concrete AI post/restoration option — local, no-cloud upscaling that recovers texture lost to compression or old codecs, restoring low-res footage to 4K. Distinct vendor/product from the published Topaz/Adobe upscaling card, adding a local-processing alternative to the same craft problem.
picks.excerpt: An AI-powered video restoration tool that upscales low-resolution footage to 4K while reducing noise and reconstructing detail, with all processing running locally on the user's machine rather than in the cloud.

dropped_as_duplicates: runway-seed-audio (Runway) — same outlet as the kept Runway Dev card and a weaker standalone (thin changelog entry, no dedicated article page). Per the at-most-one-Runway rule, dropped in favor of the bigger Runway Dev platform story.
